source.quote: MOTU's own page for the UltraLite-mk5, read 2026-11-25. Converter: « The UltraLite-mk5 includes renowned ESS Sabre32(TM) DAC technology, featuring the ES9026PRO DAC, to deliver measured 125 dB dynamic range and -114 dB THD+N. »; « 125 dB dynamic range on output ». Connections: « 1x optical in/out (ADAT or TOSLink) »; « 8-channel optical I/O »; « The optical ports alternatively support stereo TOSLink (optical S/PDIF). »; « 1x RCA S/PDIF digital in/out ». The page states NO sample rate, NO bit depth, NO DSD figure and NO digital filter. motu.com has no terms-of-use page; its only legal link is a privacy policy, which was read and restricts nothing about site content, and the footer reads « Copyright (c) 2008-2026 MOTU, Inc. All rights reserved. »

facts.chip: « ESS Sabre32 DAC technology, featuring the ES9026PRO DAC » - a part number, with the maker's own measurements beside it: « measured 125 dB dynamic range and -114 dB THD+N ».

_une_mesure_du_fabricant_et_aucun_debit: A page that publishes a MEASURED dynamic range and a THD+N figure for its own D/A path, and no sample rate at all. That inversion is characteristic of the professional segment and it is why this brand is in the catalogue: consumer makers publish ceilings and almost never measurements, pro makers publish measurements and sometimes forget the ceilings. Neither figure has a field here - the schema holds what a device ACCEPTS and nothing about how well it converts.
_une_prise_optique_qui_parle_ADAT_une_TR: « 1x optical in/out (ADAT or TOSLink) » and « 8-channel optical I/O ». Third maker in two days after the Topping E50 II and the Mytek Liberty DAC II. In the professional segment it is not a curiosity but the norm, which suggests the interface vocabulary's lack of ADAT will bite on every record this segment adds.
